title: Claude Certified Associate – Foundations (CCAO-F)

intro.about: The Claude Certified Associate – Foundations certification (exam code CCAO-F) validates that a professional can put Claude to work on real business tasks with sound judgment: writing and iterating effective prompts, evaluating and validating what comes back, choosing the right product surface and model tier, integrating Claude into workflows, configuring Projects and knowledge, using it responsibly under organizational policy, and troubleshooting when results disappoint. Exam guide version 1.0 (July 2026) defines seven content domains: Prompting and Task Execution (14%), Output Evaluation and Validation (21%), Product and Model Selection (12%), Workflow Integration and Solution Design (16%), Configuration and Knowledge Management (12%), Governance, Risk, and Responsible Use (15%), and Troubleshooting and Optimization (10%).
intro.audience: Aimed at professionals who use Claude in everyday knowledge work — the exam guide names operations, marketing, project management, education, communications and general knowledge-work roles, with limited to moderate technical expertise expected. It is explicitly not aimed at software developers building against APIs or designing agentic systems; recognizing when a task crosses into Claude Developer or Claude Architect territory and escalating it is itself part of the competency being tested. Items reward applied judgment in scenarios, not recall of definitions.

materials.title: 60-question practice exam
materials.description: Weighted to exam guide v1.0 across all seven domains and drawn from an 81-item originally-authored bank — the same item count and 120-minute length as the real sitting.

materials.title: The real exam's two formats, exactly
materials.description: Multiple choice (four options) and multiple response (five options, the stem states how many to select) — the complete CCAO-F format profile, with no formats the real exam does not use. The format coverage note below carries the full disclosure, including which values are this mock's own calibration decisions.

materials.title: Review dashboard, rationales, and a weak-rule report
materials.description: Per-domain scoring against a 72% threshold (a raw-score translation of the real exam's scaled 720-of-1,000 cut), an explanation for the key and every distractor on submission, and a weak-rule report that names which of the 35 practitioner rules behind the syllabus your misses cluster on.

intro.disclaimer: An independent, originally-authored study tool for personal exam preparation — not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to Anthropic, PBC or Pearson VUE. "Anthropic", "Claude" and "Claude Certified Associate – Foundations" are trademarks of Anthropic, PBC. Every question was written clean-room from documented derivation artefacts against the public exam guide and the author's own notes from the official prep course, with community practice material analyzed for classification only, exactly as this package's derivation records show. Nothing here is drawn from the live CCAO-F item bank: real exam content is confidential and proprietary to Anthropic and protected by the non-disclosure agreement every candidate accepts before the exam begins — which will bind you too once you sit it, so please never share live questions here.

format_coverage: The real CCAO-F exam uses two item types: multiple choice (one correct response) and multiple response, where each item states how many responses to select (exam guide v1.0 §5). There are no ordering items and no matching items. This mock's format profile is therefore a subset, not an approximation: multiple choice maps exactly to single_choice, and multiple response maps exactly to multiple_response with all-or-nothing scoring. Mockka's third format, scenario_matching, is deliberately UNUSED here (every domain sets it to 0) because authoring it would rehearse an interaction the real exam does not contain. Two disclosures follow from the guide rather than from the format set. First, the guide does not publish the option count, the select-count, or the share of multiple-response items, so this mock's values — five options, choose two, nine of sixty items — are a Mockka house decision, not a measured property of the exam; every multiple-response stem states its select-count, exactly as the guide says real items do. Second, the real exam reports a scaled score from 100 to 1,000 with a cut score of 720, set by a formal standard-setting study; that is not a percent-correct figure, and this mock's 72% pass line is a translation of it, not the vendor's threshold.
